name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection, monitoring and theorization of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network behavior on social platforms, including the CooRnet method, the VERA-AI Alert system, and studies of deceptive information operations. This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution and remains the most active strand of his work.

name: Disinformation Narratives Monitoring
description: Tracking and modeling the propagation of disinformation narratives across Europe (war in Ukraine, LGBTQI+ rights, elections) through language models and dashboards, as pursued in the PROMPT project and related fact-checking support tools.

name: Generative AI and Synthetic Media Manipulation
description: Study of how generative AI is used in coordinated manipulation campaigns (e.g., synthetic visual persuasion in gambling promotion) and of LLMs as both a threat vector and a tool for countering disinformation.

name: LLMs in Computational Content Analysis
description: Methodological work on integrating large language models into political discourse and media content analysis pipelines, including validation challenges, embedding model comparisons, and human-machine annotation workflows.

name: Platform Governance and Research Data Access
description: Research and advocacy on social media platforms' API access, data-sharing policies, and regulatory compliance (Digital Services Act, CrowdTangle shutdown, Meta's political content reduction policy, URL Shares Dataset), reflecting the researcher's role as DSA/ECAT expert.

name: Political Polarization and Partisan Media Ecosystems
description: Analysis of partisan attention, insular news consumption, hyperpartisan networks, and polarization dynamics across traditional and social media, with a strong focus on Italian elections and cross-national comparison.

name: Social Media and Elections (International Cases)
description: Comparative studies of political information campaigns and coordinated behavior around national elections outside Italy, including Brazil (post-Bolsonaro), Germany, and Latin America more broadly.

name: Health Misinformation and Coordinated Networks
description: Mapping of coordinated networks circulating problematic health content, including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration (MINE-FACTS) and cross-national studies of health misinformation in India and Nigeria.

name: Platform Engagement and Affordances
description: Research on how platform design features (reactions, algorithmic governance, virality mechanics) shape user engagement and visibility of content, including systematic reviews and conceptual work on virality.

name: Sociocybernetics and Social Systems Theory
description: Long-standing theoretical foundation in sociocybernetics and social systems theory underpinning the researcher's approach to observing complex social and media systems, maintained through ISA Research Committee 51 involvement.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.

name: Survey Measurement Validity and Comparability
description: Papers examining methodological challenges in survey-based measurement, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how online sample composition and quality checks affect representativeness and response validity, and how question wording and dataset differences affect cross-national and longitudinal comparability of trust measures.
